subject: Demo follow-up: prioritized inference strategy & landing tasks for Finvera POC
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@finvera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Demo follow-up: prioritized inference strategy & landing tasks for Finvera POC

Hi Erin — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side plus a prioritized set of model options and concrete next steps so we can ramp the PoC sprint next week. I put the lightweight prompt pack and the benchmark CSV in the attachments and a Drive link above.

TL;DR recommended shortlist (tradeoffs summarized):

1) OpenChat-40B-opt (balanced)
   - Quality: high for customer-facing summarization and extraction (meets our precision targets on the 200-sample test set: 92% top-1 accuracy for entity extraction)
   - Median p50 latency (512 tokens): ~280 ms on Dedicated c6 cluster
   - Cost: estimated $4.50 / 1M tokens (quantized float16)
   - Why: best mix of accuracy and predictable latency for Finvera’s UIs; good for structured outputs you wanted.

2) Redwood-Lite-30B-int8 (quality-oriented, quantized)
   - Quality: strongest on long-form coherence and few-shot chain-of-thought tests (higher ROUGE/F1 on internal evals)
   - Median p50 latency (512 tokens): ~360 ms (with optimized KV cache)
   - Cost: estimated $3.30 / 1M tokens (int8)
   - Tradeoff: slightly higher latency but lower per-token cost and better long-response quality. Choose if you prioritize answer quality over SLO tightness.

3) Llama2-70B-qa-quant (cost-first variant)
   - Quality: acceptable for retrieval-augmented Q&A with prompt scaffolding (87% top-1 on our quick set)
   - Median p50 latency (512 tokens): ~420 ms on general-purpose hosts
   - Cost: estimated $1.90 / 1M tokens (aggressive quant)
   - Tradeoff: best unit economics, but may need heavier prompt engineering and post-filtering for edge-case correctness.

Benchmarks: the CSV includes token-level cost extrapolations and per-model 50/95 latency points from our internal runs. Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/finvera/benchmarks_20270630

Primary risks / quality regression concerns:
- Distribution drift: the PoC sample set today skews short customer prompts; we need to validate longer real-world transcripts (we recommend running 500-case regression across your anonymized transcripts).
- Retrieval alignment: for the Q&A flows, latency can spike when RAG fetches are large; we recommend a max-context strategy and early pruning.
- Safety/PII: for payment-related fields we’ll enforce a redaction & post-processing guardrail during the eval sprint.

Recommended immediate plan (pick one model to run 2-week eval OR run two-model A/B with traffic split):
- Option A (recommended): Start with OpenChat-40B-opt single-model eval (2 weeks).
- Option B: Run OpenChat-40B-opt + Llama2-70B cost variant as A/B to measure cost/quality tradeoffs on production-like traffic (2 weeks).

Concrete next steps / owners (proposed):
- Sofía: spin up the eval harness and deploy models to a sandbox Dedicated cluster (ETA: Mon 7/5).
- Ben: run the 500-case regression with your redacted transcripts and report back on distribution gaps (ETA: Wed 7/7).
- Monica: produce a concise procurement checklist for PII/data-residency controls we discussed (ETA: Tue 7/6).
- Erin / Finvera: confirm whether you want single-model (Option A) or A/B (Option B) and share the set of 500 transcripts (anonymized) or point us to a secure S3 bucket (ETA: Fri 7/2).

Attachments: finvera_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt pack + short instructions), benchmarks_finvera_20270630.csv, mutual_action_plan_finvera.docx

Open items for your call next week: latency SLO target (is 300ms p50 for 512 tokens acceptable?), data residency boundary for logs, and procurement cadence.

Thanks again — happy to jump on another quick call if you want to walk the benchmark CSV together.

— Sofía

Thanks, Sofia — solid summary. Two quick notes:

1) I’ll own the regression run but want to flag that Ben (me) will need a small mapping script to normalize the timestamps/utterance boundaries in Finvera transcripts; please include that in the prompt pack (Monica can add as an attachment).

2) Security ask: loop in Security (I suggest cc’ing "security_ops@redwood.ai") before we pull any S3 objects. We also should plan to run the 500-case regression in our VPC sandbox to avoid export.

+1 on starting with OpenChat-40B-opt unless Erin pushes hard on cost.

— Ben

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: prioritized inference strategy & landing tasks for Finvera POC

Sofía / team — thanks for the clear options. We’re inclined to start with Option A (OpenChat-40B-opt) and run a 2-week single-model eval. A few questions/asks from procurement and engineering:

- Latency SLO: Can you confirm 95th percentile for 256 tokens and 512 tokens? We are targeting a UI perception target of 300ms p50 for 512 tokens but want to see p95 numbers for alerting.
- SOC2 / compliance: procurement needs the SOC2 report and the data-retention policy before we share transcripts. Please send the appropriate evidence or a pointer to the compliance pack.
- PO/procurement: procurement@finvera.com will start the paperwork — can you share a short commercial MOP (order-of-operations) and estimated monthly burn for the pilot if we scale to ~500k tokens/month?

We will aim to provide the redacted 500-case set by Friday 7/2 and will share an S3 read-only path if you prefer.

Thanks — Erin
Erin Walsh
Head of Product, Finvera

Great — thanks Erin. Confirming execution plan and owners:

1) OpenChat-40B-opt single-model eval (2 weeks) — deploy to Dedicated sandbox cluster (Sofía) by Mon 7/5.
2) Regression run (Ben) on the 500-case redacted set (to be provided via read-only S3). Ben will post the summary and a short list of distribution mismatches by Wed 7/7.
3) Compliance artifacts: Monica will push the SOC2 extract, data retention and KMS integration notes to the Drive folder and to procurement@finvera.com by Tue 7/6.
4) Latency metrics: I’ll run a gated benchmark for p50/p95 at 256/512 tokens and post numbers to the shared Drive (ETA: Tue 7/6). Preliminary p95 estimates from today's sandbox runs: 256 tokens p95 ~ 340 ms, 512 tokens p95 ~ 470 ms (we’ll provide full histograms).
5) Commercial MOP & pilot burn: Ben will draft an expected cost run-rate for 500k tokens/month with burst assumptions and attach to the mutual_action_plan_finvera.docx.

If that timeline looks good I’ll schedule a quick 30-minute check-in for Wed 7/7 to review regression results and the latency histograms.

— Sofía
